subject: Post-call recap: performance SLOs + customer-led load test (Fathom Analytics)
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Ramirez <sofia@fathomanalytics.com>, ops@fathomanalytics.com
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: performance SLOs + customer-led load test (Fathom Analytics)

Hi Sofia / Fathom ops team —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so everyone is aligned for the customer-led load test: 

Recap of targets we discussed
- Latency SLOs (generation endpoint, 512-token average payload): p50 < 80ms, p95 < 250ms, p99 < 500ms under steady-state traffic
- Throughput target: sustained 1200 tokens/sec aggregate for the test window (equates to roughly 20 concurrent non-streaming sessions or ~200 concurrent streaming sessions depending on client chunking)
- Streaming requirements: support 200 concurrent streaming sessions with max per-session single-token latency < 120ms after connection warm-up
- KV-cache expectations: clients will re-use a short prefix (average 30 tokens) — we expect cache-hit benefit in steady-state

Test scaffold & tooling
- Customer-led framework: you indicated a preference for k6 for HTTP streaming and Locust-like scenarios for open-loop bursts. We attached a k6 sample (k6-sample-streaming.js) and an SLO matrix (fathom_slo_matrix.xlsx) that maps test scenarios to success criteria.
- Test accounts: Redwood will provision a sandbox API key scoped to the test project and restrict access by CIDR allowlist.
- IP allowlist: please confirm the public egress ranges at your end; our infra requires the egress CIDRs to create allowlist entries. Proposed Redwood CIDRs to allow: 34.82.0.0/16, 35.196.0.0/16 (we will provide final single-IP endpoints before the run).

Proposed windows (please confirm):
- Preferred: Tue 2027-06-01 09:00–11:00 PT (primary window)
- Backup: Wed 2027-06-02 14:00–16:00 PT

Action items & owners
- Rachel (me): coordinate test window, send sandbox account/credentials instructions, finalize allowlist entries once your egress list is received.
- Marcus (SE): review the k6 script for streaming chunking behavior and provide an annotated version for Fathom.
- Connor (SRE): validate internal routing and prepare a light monitoring dashboard (latency histograms + connection counts).
- Sofia / Fathom ops: share egress IP list, confirm preferred window, and let us know which scenarios (burst vs sustained vs mixed streaming) you want prioritized.

Attachments: fathom_slo_matrix.xlsx, k6-sample-streaming.js, sandbox_key_instructions.txt

If the proposed primary window works, we’ll provision the sandbox key and firewall entries 48 hours prior and run a short smoke test 1 hour before start. 

Thanks — looking forward to the run.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Sofia Ramirez <sofia@fathomanalytics.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: ops@fathomanalytics.com, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 18:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: performance SLOs + customer-led load test (Fathom Analytics)

Thanks Rachel — this is great, appreciate the clarity. A few quick notes from our side: 

- We prefer k6 for everything if possible; our ops team can adapt Locust scenarios if you need them but k6 is the org standard.
- We'll share our egress CIDRs by EOD tomorrow (ops@fathomanalytics.com will send the list).
- Primary window (Tue 2027-06-01 09:00–11:00 PT) works for our engineering and SRE teams. Please schedule the smoke test at 08:00 PT so we can validate connectivity.
- For scenario priority: 1) sustained streaming at target concurrency, 2) ramp/burst test to validate fallback, 3) long-tail p99 chase with larger payloads.

Can you confirm how token accounting is reflected in the sample script? We want to ensure our client-side chunking matches your streaming chunk-size assumptions.

Sofia Ramirez
Head of Platform Engineering | Fathom Analytics
sofia@fathomanalytics.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Ramirez <sofia@fathomanalytics.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 07:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: performance SLOs + customer-led load test (Fathom Analytics)

Hi all — quick technical clarifications: 

- Token accounting: the k6-sample-streaming.js includes a helper that estimates tokens on the client by splitting on whitespace and punctuation; for the run we'll provide a mapping that uses a byte-based estimator to be conservative. If Fathom has its own tokenizer we can wire a small RPC to return counts during the smoke test.
- Streaming chunk size: we expect clients to flush chunks of ~8–16 tokens; smaller chunks increase per-token overhead. I’ll annotate the script (attached) with comments showing where to change chunking and simulated thinking delays.
- Sandbox key: Rachel — please include the sandbox key instructions but do not post raw keys via email. We’ll provision the test key in the console and share retrieval instructions.

I’ll upload an annotated k6 script to the shared Drive link by 10:00 PT. Connor and I will also provision an ephemeral Prometheus scrape target for the smoke test so Fathom can join the dashboard.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Ramirez <sofia@fathomanalytics.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: performance SLOs + customer-led load test (Fathom Analytics)

Thanks — quick scheduling update and next steps: 

- Window confirmed: Tue 2027-06-01 09:00–11:00 PT. Smoke test at 08:00 PT.
- Sofia / ops team: we received your CIDR list (ops@fathomanalytics.com) and created provisional allowlist entries for the two service IP ranges. We will replace those with single-IP endpoints 24 hours before the run.
- Marcus: thanks — please drop the annotated script and the conservative token-mapping file into the Drive link and flag any changes in the k6 scenario names so we can tag metrics correctly.
- Connor: please enable the temporary dashboard and retention for 72 hours post-run (we'll need the histograms for the post-mortem).

Logistics note about error budgets/rollback: if p95 exceeds 350ms for more than 5 consecutive minutes during sustained scenarios we will exercise an automatic throttling policy and discuss next steps with Fathom on the call. That behavior is in the SLO matrix under "Automated fallback".

I'll follow up with the sandbox provisioning timeline and a short checklist for the smoke test. Looking forward to running this with you all.

Cheers,
Rachel
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com
